$comment: A mock Jira project, so you can try pulling without credentials. Epics group stories through `epic`. A real Jira returns the same shape from the jira reader in server.mjs.
name: Jira

items.title: Workbench Web: review changes in the browser
items.description:
Let people review what a feature's session changed without leaving Workbench Web: a diff view, per-file navigation and a way to send review notes back to the session.

Out of scope: committing or pushing from the browser.

items.title: Show the project's git diff next to the transcript
items.description:
Add a 'Changes' tab next to the transcript that shows `git diff` for the project, refreshed after each turn. Read-only is fine.

Acceptance criteria:
- The tab shows added and removed lines with colour and line numbers.
- It refreshes when a turn ends.
- An empty diff says 'No changes'.

items.title: Jump between changed files in the diff view
items.description:
List the changed files above the diff; clicking one scrolls to it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Files show added/removed line counts.
- Works at phone width.

items.title: Send a review note on a diff line to the session
items.description:
Clicking a diff line opens a small note box; sending it posts a message to the feature's session quoting the file, line and note.

Acceptance criteria:
- The message includes file path and line number.
- Works whether the session is running or stopped (stopped sessions resume).

items.title: Landing site polish
items.description: Small improvements to the Workbench landing page in site/ before it is shared more widely.

items.title: Add a light/dark theme toggle
items.description:
The landing page in site/ follows the OS colour scheme only. Add a small toggle in the nav that remembers the choice in localStorage and falls back to the OS setting. Keep it dependency-free.

Acceptance criteria:
- Works at desktop and phone widths.
- No flash of the wrong theme on load.

items.title: Add an FAQ section
items.description: Add an FAQ to site/index.html answering: Does it need an API key? Where is agent state stored? Can teammates share features? Use <details> elements and match the existing card style.

items.title: Auto-approve read-only tool requests
items.description:
Use the policy hook in workbench-web/policy.mjs to auto-approve clearly safe requests (read-only git commands to start) and still ask for anything uncertain.

Acceptance criteria:
- Denied and uncertain requests still reach the browser.
- Every automatic decision is shown in the transcript.
